incidents.vector: A single suspected advanced actor exploited a critical vCenter directory-traversal flaw (CVE-2026-59310, CVSS 9.8) for remote code execution within five days of its July 29 disclosure, then planted reverse_ssh outbound channels for persistence.
incidents.impact: Incident responder QUIRSO traced activity to 361 unique IP addresses across 47 nations, with the US, France, Iran, and Turkey most heavily hit; the reverse_ssh persistence survives patching, so patched-but-compromised systems remain under attacker control.

incidents.victim: Governments, military, telecom, and a US aerospace manufacturer
incidents.vector: The 'Jewelbug' mercenary group ran both espionage and crypto theft from one custom C2 panel (XG-Web), using Windows/Linux backdoors and a malicious 'PDF Viewer' browser extension that harvests cookies, session tokens, and credentials; in one case it planted a script in a state telecom's webmail platform.
incidents.impact: Symantec found 580,000+ browser cookie jars, 2,300 exfiltrated email bodies, and thousands of credentials across government, military, police, and telecom victims in Asia and the Middle East, plus a major US industrial/aerospace manufacturer, while simultaneously running 44 servers of fake crypto exchanges.

incidents.victim: Goodwin Procter, WilmerHale, and other law firms
incidents.vector: The 'Silent Ransom' (Luna Moth) group phishes and, increasingly, impersonates IT support staff in person to install legitimate remote-access software, then rapidly exfiltrates sensitive data — often start to finish within a single day.
incidents.impact: Two law firms paid multimillion-dollar ransoms this year — Goodwin Procter reportedly $10 million and WilmerHale $18 million — as the group leverages the reputational threat of leaked attorney-client data against reputation-based firms.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack took down the court's internal systems, part of a broader wave of ransomware targeting Latin American government institutions.
incidents.impact: The internal systems of Guatemala's Supreme Court were knocked offline, disrupting judicial operations.

incidents.victim: Routers and edge devices (Alcatel, D-Link, Netgear, Tenda, others)
incidents.vector: A previously undocumented Linux/Mirai-derived botnet dubbed Evooo1Bot exploits unpatched vulnerabilities in internet-facing hardware, adding encrypted C2, honeypot-aware SSH scanning, a default-credential sniffer, and SOCKS-proxy abuse.
incidents.impact: FortiGuard Labs reports at least a month of active exploitation concentrated in North and South America, Europe, India, China, and Japan; compromised devices become persistent proxies that let attackers hide their origin and pivot into internal networks.

incidents.victim: Taiwan government and Thailand Ministry of Finance
incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese hackers chained open-source AI frameworks (Hermes and OpenClaw) into a multi-agent system that ran autonomous 'Learning Cycles' — searching vulnerability databases and repos to adapt mid-operation — after bypassing model guardrails by framing the work as authorized penetration testing.
incidents.impact: In what researchers call the first known near-autonomous AI attack on a government target, the framework extracted 2,500+ personnel records and expanded on its own to IT supply-chain vendors, a nuclear safety agency, a government email system, and 7+ energy companies; the same campaign breached Thailand's finance ministry.

incidents.victim: Defense, aerospace, and aviation job applicants
incidents.vector: As part of Operation 'Dream Job', North Korean operators posed as recruiters for Lockheed Martin and Enveil on LinkedIn, sent malicious PDFs with a trojanized reader, and exploited a Windows Winsock zero-day (CVE-2026-68820) to escalate to full system control.
incidents.impact: The actively exploited flaw — the only confirmed in-the-wild bug in Microsoft's 400-plus August patch batch — gave attackers long-term remote access to victims in France, Germany, Brazil, and India; CISA ordered federal agencies to patch by August 25.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian IT professionals and system administrators
incidents.vector: GRU sub-group UAC-0145 scours job portals, contacts IT professionals via Telegram to arrange fake job interviews, and delivers Windows or Linux malware through the 'test tasks' candidates are asked to download.
incidents.impact: CERT-UA says the campaign, running since May, aims to harvest credentials from compromised admins and pivot into the companies and government networks they manage to collect battlefield-relevant intelligence.

incidents.vector: The 'City-Forum' actor built custom tooling to probe overly permissive guest-access settings, reaching undocumented interfaces such as Salesforce's Lightning Web Runtime data-access layer and an obscure ServiceNow Service Portal search endpoint.
incidents.impact: Active since at least March 2025, the campaign has targeted telecom, financial services, enterprise software, security, and public-sector organizations across North America, Europe, and Asia, potentially exposing account, contact, and document data left accessible to anonymous users.

incidents.vector: Hackers claimed to exploit an XXE (XML external entity) vulnerability to breach the healthcare platform and steal customer files and source code.
incidents.impact: The platform, used by Polish hospitals, allegedly stores data on nearly 19 million Poles; the stolen data is now being sold online while authorities investigate.

incidents.vector: Attackers repeatedly exploited an unpatched, publicly documented flaw in ACRO's internet-facing Kentico portal (unpatched since 2019), and in one incident used SQL injection to expose employee credentials; antivirus alerts, including quarantined Mimikatz detections, went unread.
incidents.impact: The UK ICO reprimanded ACRO after three intrusions between July 2021 and June 2023 went undetected for nearly two years, staging the sensitive data of ~11,000 people for exfiltration and prompting notification of 84,000+ applicants; the Medusa ransomware group claimed responsibility.

incidents.victim: Android TV boxes and IoT/edge devices
incidents.vector: The Kimwolf/Aisuru DDoS botnet's v7 adds an HTTP/2 flood that mimics full Chrome browser fingerprints to evade filtering, and moves C2 resolution to the Ethereum Name Service (five public RPC endpoints) with a Tor .onion fallback to survive takedowns.
incidents.impact: Palo Alto Unit 42 says the takedown-resistant variant, active since February with infrastructure traced to Saint Petersburg, Russia, spreads via unauthenticated Android Debug Bridge and powers hard-to-block DDoS attacks against websites.

incidents.vector: As part of North Korea's remote IT-worker scheme, an operative passed identity-proofing and background checks to be hired as a contract IT employee for a federal agency.
incidents.impact: The FBI is investigating after discovering the worker in late July; it is unclear how long the intrusion lasted, what agency was affected, or whether sensitive data was accessed.

incidents.victim: Government, critical infrastructure, and healthcare organizations worldwide
incidents.vector: Gunra is a ransomware-as-a-service operation whose affiliates use a double-extortion model — encrypting data and threatening to publish or sell exfiltrated files — while deleting logs and clearing command history to hinder detection.
incidents.impact: NSA, FBI, and partners issued a joint #StopRansomware advisory; Gunra victims span the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific across healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, transportation, government, and utilities.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained access to the French shipping and logistics firm's systems and began leaking stolen customer data on the dark web.
incidents.impact: The breach rippled across at least eight European warehouses and downstream companies including Valve's Steam hardware business and Dutch retailers Bol and De Bijenkorf, exposing customer names, addresses, phone numbers, and emails and causing days- to weeks-long delivery delays.

incidents.vector: Attackers used social engineering to breach employee computers and access corporate data.
incidents.impact: Levi Strauss disclosed that hackers compromised employee machines and reached corporate data; the full scope of accessed information was still being assessed.

incidents.victim: npm ecosystem (400+ packages, incl. keyv, cacheable-request)
incidents.vector: The self-propagating 'ChainDrop' worm adds a preinstall hook that drops an obfuscated payload run via the legitimate Bun runtime; it steals npm/GitHub tokens to republish additional packages and scrapes OIDC tokens directly from GitHub Actions runner memory.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 found ChainDrop infected 400+ packages downloaded hundreds of millions of times weekly, stealing cloud credentials, SSH keys, and developer secrets across 10+ environments and persisting via VS Code and Claude Code hooks; on Aug 4 the operator silently reconfigured C2 via a single Ethereum transaction. The worm skips Russian-language hosts.

incidents.victim: Financial, private equity, and legal firms (incl. Wall Street targets)
incidents.vector: UNC6671 (rebranded from BlackFile to Redact, and linked to Pink, Helix, and Falcon leak sites) runs high-volume IT-helpdesk voice phishing, luring employees on personal phones to passkey-themed lookalike portals that use adversary-in-the-middle infrastructure to steal credentials and MFA tokens, then exfiltrates data from Microsoft 365 and Okta.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence Group says the actor shifted targeting through 2026 to private equity, law firms, and financial rating agencies; Reuters reported attempted attacks on major hedge funds and PE firms, and blockchain analysis tied over $10 million in ransom payments to the group's wallets.

incidents.vector: In the 2024 campaign, Connor Moucka ('Judische') and co-conspirators used stolen credentials to access Snowflake customer accounts that lacked multi-factor authentication, then extorted victims by threatening to publish the data.
incidents.impact: Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud, wire fraud, aggravated identity theft, and conspiracy for breaching 165+ organizations and stealing call/text records of 100M+ AT&T customers; the conspirators collected over $2.5 million in ransoms, and he faces up to decades in prison at October sentencing.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack disrupted operations at North Carolina's ports; the intrusion vector has not been publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: State officials and the US Coast Guard are investigating the attack, which was reported 'contained'; port operations were disrupted during the incident.

incidents.vector: Hackers stole patient data from third-party cloud systems used by the company.
incidents.impact: Biotech giant Amgen disclosed that patient data was taken from third-party cloud systems, joining a run of breaches tied to cloud and supply-chain exposure.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack struck part of the ministry's technology infrastructure, encrypting files and degrading public-facing services, one day after Colombia's national CERT warned of heightened ransomware focus on the country.
incidents.impact: The attack, five days before the nation's presidential handover, disrupted illicit-drug monitoring and legal-process services; officials said some files were encrypted but denied data was stolen, part of a broader surge of attacks on Colombian and Latin American government bodies.
